items.stem: Explain why each adjustment listed below a trial balance affects two items in the financial statements.
items.answer: Each adjustment is a double entry: one effect is in the income statement (income or expense) and the other in the statement of financial position (asset or liability).

items.stem: Explain why the depreciation charge is not shown in the trial balance.
items.answer: It is calculated at the year end after the trial balance is extracted, from the asset cost or carrying amount and the policy.
items.markingKey: Calculated at year end [1]; after TB [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the closing capital in the statement of financial position must equal net assets.
items.answer: By the accounting equation, assets − liabilities = capital; profit increases net assets and capital equally, drawings reduce both.

items.stem: Explain why both the income statement and the statement of financial position are needed by users.
items.answer: The income statement shows performance over the year; the SFP shows the financial position (assets, liabilities, capital) at a point in time.
items.markingKey: IS – performance over period [1]; SFP – position at a date [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways a sole trader could improve working capital.
items.answer: Introduce more capital; take a long-term loan; sell surplus non-current assets; reduce drawings; collect receivables faster; reduce inventory.
